passage.text: Therapists often find themselves caught in the same relational pattern, and they feel impulses to repeat the reactions that others typically show toward depressed people. For example, a therapist may try to encourage the client with well-intended practical suggestions for changing stressful life conditions. They then experience frustration or irritation when the client is unable to make any change. However, their awareness gives therapists the opportunity to step out of this rigid relational pattern and respond differently to the depressed person. They remain available for contact, they do not blame either themselves or the client, and they do not give up hope. In doing this, therapists change the usual rigid organization of the field and open a space for change for their client as well.
